prose.overview: Asherah is the face of the game: noble, impulsive and carrying a sword that was sealed for very good reasons. In a team she plays like you'd expect, an area damage dealer who needs a few turns to get going. I like her, but I wouldn't build a roster around her.
prose.basic: Stranis Style Slash is a 65% ATK poke. Treat it as a Chill generator, because every stack feeds Veil Cleave.
prose.special: Veil Cleave hits all enemies for 200% ATK (AoE damage is split between targets, so think roughly 50% each), gives you SPD Up for 2 turns and does 30% extra when Chill is full. It starts on a 5-turn cooldown and drops to 3 with the level 6 and 10 upgrades, which makes it the upgrade to buy first.
prose.ult: Dawn of Night is the heavier swing: 210% ATK on everyone, CRIT DMG Up for 2 turns and two Chill. The 6-turn cooldown (4 after upgrades) means you open a wave with it and let Veil Cleave cover the gaps.
prose.passive: The passive is where she grows. It starts as +15% ATK. From passive level 2 she also gets +30% CRIT Rate when she attacks and +6% CRIT DMG per attack, stacking to 5. That's +30% CRIT DMG by the fifth hit, so long fights suit her and quick ones don't.
prose.closing: She's a fine early carry and a poor long-term plan. If you pulled her, use her. If you didn't, don't lose sleep.
prose.dupes: About dupes: ignore them for now. Stars give flat stat bumps (+2% each, +14% max) and never unlock skills.

prose.overview: Smile brings a handmade cannon called Happy End and a cat that does most of the thinking. The kit is a loop: shoot, build Leap, trigger a free area hit, repeat. It's cute and it works, but it works best on tougher single targets and is easy to outgrow.
prose.basic: Firing Coordinates Confirmed is a 50% ATK shot that gives 1 Leap. She also fills 15% of her action gauge when it lands, and another 15% if the target is at or below 50% HP.
prose.special: Cat Tapdance isn't a button, it fires by itself. If the enemy you just shot is still alive at 50% HP or less, it hits everyone for 120% ATK with a Burn attempt (75% chance, 100% at level 10) and adds a Smile Matrix stack, which is 5% ATK each, up to ten. Cooldown is just 1 turn.
prose.ult: All Units, Open Fire! is 115% ATK on one enemy with a guaranteed DEF Down for 2 turns, plus 3 Leap and another Smile Matrix. It's cooldown 6, 4 after upgrades. The DEF Down is the part your whole team enjoys.
prose.passive: Happy Trigger starts as +15% ATK. From passive level 2, full Leap after a basic spends the stacks and fires Cat Tapdance, and her basic gives 9% plus 9% turn progress (up to 15% plus 15% at max). In plain terms: shoot more, act more.
prose.closing: Good on a budget and fun to play. Just don't expect her to carry hard content on her own.

prose.overview: Carnelia transforms dark magic into crows and then sends the crows to do her job. She hits the whole room, shoves enemy turn gauges backwards and refuses to die the first time. Almost half of top-100 Gauntlet squads have her, which tells you what the people who climb think of crows.¶Wanderer is her title, and it fits the playstyle: she's always moving. Every skill gives her Agitation, Agitation gives her ATK, her ultimate gives her turn progress and her passive gives her a second life. The more she acts, the stronger she gets, and she acts a lot.
prose.basic: Gesture of Dawn is 65% ATK and gives her 1 Agitation. Each Agitation stack gives her +6% ATK at max passive (2% at first), up to 5 stacks, which is +30% ATK at the top.¶It's downtime filler, and it isn't a way to re-apply Umbral Echo. Use it to top up Agitation when both skills are on cooldown. The Nova Burst adds 1 Toughness damage.
prose.special: Guiding Twilight is 70% ATK on one enemy, with a 100% Buff Block for 2 turns at max level (75% at first, 85% at level 4) and -25% enemy turn gauge. It also gives her 1 Agitation. With Umbral Echo up, it repeats once on a random enemy, once per turn. Cooldown 4, then 3 at level 6.¶It's a damage skill that also steals tempo. Buff Block stops the enemy from using buffs, which is brutal against bosses that rely on them. You can't pick the repeat's target, so don't count on it for a specific enemy.
prose.ult: Dissonance Break is 265% ATK on all enemies, +30% of her own turn gauge at max level (15% at first) and +50% damage when she has Umbral Echo. It adds 1 Agitation. The Nova Burst heals her for 15% of the damage dealt and adds 1 Toughness damage. Cooldown 5, then 4 at level 6.¶That 50% bonus is the whole reason to hold her ultimate until Umbral Echo is active. She starts the fight with 1 turn of Umbral Echo, so the opening ultimate is already boosted.
prose.passive: Spoke gives +15% ATK and Umbral Echo for 1 turn at the start of battle. Agitation adds ATK on attack, and then comes the fun clause: once per battle a lethal hit leaves her at 1% HP with 1 turn of Immortality, 3 turns of Umbral Echo and all cooldowns reset.¶That's a free second life plus a free reset on your ultimate. It doesn't revive a dead ally, it just refuses to let her die the first time. Rude. Enemies don't know when it'll happen, which makes her tough to plan against in PvP.
prose.closing: Level the ultimate first, then the Special. Build crit, keep Umbral Echo up and let the crows work.
prose.dupes: Dupes? Optional. Every star adds +2% ATK, HP and DEF (+14% at 7 stars) and never touches the kit, so they are a whale bonus, not a requirement.
prose.play: Open with the ultimate while Umbral Echo is up for the +50% hit and the turn progress. After that, alternate Guiding Twilight and the basic to build Agitation and slow the enemy. When she's close to dying, don't panic: once per battle the passive saves her and resets everything, so the next turn is an ultimate.¶Keep Umbral Echo up. It's what gives her ultimate +50% and doubles her Special. If it falls off, try to get a turn where it's active before you use the ultimate. Don't waste the Special on a target that doesn't have buffs unless you need the turn gauge shove.
prose.gear: Strength first, Vitality second, Focus third. Gear: ATK%, CRIT Rate, CRIT DMG, SPD, with Effect Hit useful for Buff Block. Attack (4) or Destruction (4) sets. Upgrade the ultimate first (level 4 and 8 add turn gauge gain, level 6 cuts cooldown), then the Special (level 4 and 8 raise Buff Block chance to 100%, level 6 cuts cooldown), then the passive. The basic gets only small bumps, so leave it.

prose.overview: Emily is a maid with a very large broom and the calm of someone who has seen it all. She's the first support I hand to any beginner. She soaks hits, gives your damage dealer a Barrier and an ATK buff, and somehow does it without wasting her own turn. Easy to build, very hard to dislike.¶A Defender who also buffs is rare. Most tanks only absorb damage. Emily absorbs damage, puts a shield on your carry and then reuses her turn. That's why she's S+ in PvE and a default pick for Moon teams.
prose.basic: Commence Combat Cleanup is 50% ATK plus 3.5% of her max HP, and it adds 1 Chill. The max HP scaling means HP gear helps her damage too. That's a gift for a character whose job isn't damage.¶The Nova Burst adds 1 Toughness damage and gives her a 1-turn Barrier. It isn't a heal, so don't expect it to save a failing team. It's just a safe filler.
prose.special: Cleaning Service gives one ally ATK Up and a Barrier (based on her HP) for 3 turns. Then she gets 3 Chill and an extra turn. The target doesn't get the extra turn, she does. Cooldown 5, then 4 at level 6.¶The buff is free tempo-wise. For the record: despite the name, it doesn't remove debuffs. Put it on your carry. The 3 Chill is the fuel for her ultimate's cooldown reduction.
prose.ult: Turn-Down Service is 170% ATK plus 10% max HP on all enemies and gives the whole team DEF Up for 2 turns. At full Chill it resets the Chill and cuts its own cooldown by 2. Each Awakened Memory stack adds 50% damage to it, up to 3. The cooldown is 8, then 7 at level 6.¶Eight turns sounds awful, but her passive and her Chill make it much shorter in practice. A fresh Memory doesn't boost the cast that gives it, so the first use is the weakest and the third is the strongest.
prose.passive: Ready Maid is +15% max HP (grows from 5%) and a Barrier at the start of the first battle. Each hit she takes cuts Turn-Down Service's cooldown by 1, and an attack on the whole team cuts another 1 and may add Chill (50% at first, 100% at max). Getting hit is a feature.¶That's what makes the 8-turn cooldown fine. In a fight where enemies target her, the ultimate comes back in a couple of turns. If she isn't being hit, her cooldown crawls, so keep her in front.
prose.closing: The default tank for most Moon teams. If you only invest in one Defender, make it her. Special first, because that's where the Barrier and the ATK Up live.
prose.dupes: On dupes: not needed. A star is +2% ATK, HP and DEF and nothing else, so her value comes from the kit at 0 stars.
prose.play: Turn one: Cleaning Service on your carry, then she gets her extra turn to follow up with the ultimate or the basic. Chill from the Special plus her passive means the ultimate can come back quickly: use it when Chill is full to cut its cooldown by 2.¶Keep Cleaning Service rolling whenever it's ready, because ATK Up and the Barrier last 3 turns and the cooldown is only 5 (4 later). In between, use the basic to fill gaps. Don't hold the ultimate for stacks: use it, build another Memory and repeat.
prose.gear: Vitality first, Endurance second, Strength third. Gear: HP%, DEF%, SPD, Effect RES. Armor DEF and Gauntlets HP as main stats, Amulet and Ring HP% or DEF%. A Health (4) set is the default, and Speed (4) works if she needs to act first. Upgrade Cleaning Service first, since the Barrier grows with each level and level 6 cuts the cooldown. Then Turn-Down Service (level 6 cooldown cut), then the passive (levels 2 to 4 strengthen it), then the basic.

prose.overview: Frey is the quartermaster who negotiates everything, including your survival. She's the Kingdom version, so don't confuse her with the Bunny girl who happens to share her name. Put her in a Star team, keep her alive and your carry will stop dying to poison.
prose.basic: Negotiation Failed is 40% ATK and 1 Leap. With a Nova Burst it puts a Barrier on your lowest-HP ally, which is a nice bonus for a basic attack.
prose.special: Rapid Resupply heals one ally based on her max HP and wipes all their debuffs, with extra healing for Star allies. It adds 2 Leap and has a cooldown of just 3, so you can use it a lot. It's the best cleanse she has.
prose.ult: Monastir's All-Out Support heals everyone, gives a 3-turn Barrier and 2 turns of Effect RES Up, and adds 2 Leap. Cooldown 6, 5 with upgrades. Save it for the moment everyone is low, not for opening.
prose.passive: No-Loss Deal begins as +15% max HP growth. From passive level 2 she gains a Leap every turn, and when her basic hits full Leap she spends the stacks, heals everyone and moves 30% closer to her next turn. Her ultimate also gives all allies 9 to 15% turn progress if someone is at 75% HP or lower.
prose.closing: Good sustain if you're building Star. Otherwise Waltz Asherah just does the job with more polish.
prose.dupes: About dupes: don't chase them. Seven stars give +14% ATK, HP and DEF in total and no new skills.

prose.overview: Lyn's two main skills are named Phantom Blade Dance and Clear Wind Bright Moon. The sect has a naming department and I don't want to argue with it. The loop is simple once you've seen it: one skill sets up the other, and the other sets up your team.¶She has two modes. In one, she buffs the Star team and spreads Leap. In the other, she goes single-target with extra crit damage. Which mode you're in depends on which skill you cast first, and that's the entire learning curve.
prose.basic: Fivefold Slash is 65% ATK and gives her 1 Leap. Leap raises her ATK by 2% to 4% per stack when she attacks (up to 5 stacks), and does a small bonus against Moon enemies. The Nova Burst adds 1 Toughness damage and SPD Up for 1 turn.¶The basic is how you refill Leap if you're short. It's not exciting, but a full Leap bar is up to +20% ATK.
prose.special: Phantom Blade Dance is 160% ATK on all enemies, cooldown 5. If she has Clear Wind, all Star allies get 3 Leap. If she doesn't, she gets ATK Up and Bright Moon for 3 turns, and an extra turn if Clear Wind Bright Moon is ready.¶So the skill does two different things depending on what she has. Without Clear Wind it's a self-buff that starts the burst mode. With Clear Wind it's a team buff that spreads Leap to every Star ally.
prose.ult: Clear Wind Bright Moon is 210% ATK on all enemies, cooldown 5. With Bright Moon it hits one target instead, with +50% CRIT DMG and 1 extra Toughness damage. Without Bright Moon, all other Star allies get CRIT DMG Up for 2 turns and she gets 3 turns of Clear Wind (a SPD buff). She gets an extra turn if Phantom Blade Dance can be used.¶Two skills, two states, one big sword. The ultimate is both an area attack with a team buff and a single-target crit nuke, depending on whether Bright Moon is on.
prose.passive: Blade Dancer is +15% ATK and +2% to 4% ATK per Leap, up to 5 stacks. Her own-turn Phantom Blade Dance with Clear Wind cuts its cooldown by 1, and the same goes for Clear Wind Bright Moon with Bright Moon. They're not unconditional refreshes, only state-based ones.¶It's a loop that accelerates the longer it runs. Keeping the right state active lets her cast both skills more often.
prose.closing: Level the passive first, since it speeds up both skills. Great in a Star team and merely good without one. Learn the loop on an easy stage.
prose.dupes: About dupes: ignore them for now. Stars give flat stat bumps (+2% each, +14% max) and never unlock skills.
prose.play: Pick a mode. For a team buff turn: cast the ultimate first without Bright Moon. That gives your Star allies CRIT DMG Up and her Clear Wind, plus an extra turn if the Special is ready. Then the Special with Clear Wind gives all Star allies 3 Leap.¶For a burst turn: cast the Special first without Clear Wind. That gives her ATK Up and Bright Moon, plus an extra turn if the ultimate is ready. Then the ultimate with Bright Moon hits one target with +50% CRIT DMG. Use the buff mode on groups and the burst mode on bosses.
prose.gear: Strength first, Vitality second, Endurance third. Gear: ATK%, CRIT Rate, CRIT DMG, SPD. Attack (4) or Destruction (4) sets. Upgrade the passive first (levels 2 to 4 raise the ATK per Leap and strengthen the loop), then the ultimate, then the Special, then the basic. She has no cooldown cuts on her skills, so the passive does the speeding up.

incognita-landgrave.author: Rook
incognita-landgrave.take: A Sun gunslinger who burns the whole enemy team once your allies have charged her up. Every skill is named after a grudge.

prose.overview: Look at her skill names: Vengeance and Retribution, Seething Vengeance, Nightmare Unleashed, Festering Resentment. Cristelle is not subtle about being upset. She's a Sun Ranger who sets the enemy on fire whenever your team has charged her up, then shoots them harder for every debuff they're carrying. A walking grudge with a pistol, and a good one.¶She's a team player more than a solo carry. Her reaction depends on allies attacking, and the Ignition she hands out makes other Sun allies better too. Put her in a Sun team that attacks every turn and she's an S-tier engine.
prose.basic: Vengeance and Retribution is 65% ATK and gives her 1 Ignition. Her passive fills 30% of her turn gauge after it at max level (18% at first). If the target has a debuff she also adds Chain DMG based on her ATK, 100% of the time.¶The Nova Burst adds 1 Toughness damage and a 100% chance to Burn for 2 turns, and it ignores Effect RES. So the basic is also a debuff source if you spend a Nova Burst on it.
prose.special: Seething Vengeance is a reaction. When another ally attacks and she's at max Ignition, it fires on its own. 100% chance to inflict 2 Burn on all enemies for 2 turns (75% at first), +30% to 50% turn progress, Drive for Revenge for 3 turns (more ATK and Effect Hit) and 2 Ignition to every other Sun ally. Her own Ignition resets to zero. Cooldown 4, then 3 at level 6.¶The more your team attacks with Specials and Ultimates, the more often it goes off. It's her main debuff source, and the debuffs are what the ultimate cashes in on.
prose.ult: Nightmare Unleashed is 90% ATK on one enemy, extends Burn by 1 turn and deals Chain DMG (based on her ATK) for each debuff on it, up to 5. It fills 30% of her turn gauge. Cooldown 4, then 3 at level 6.¶It doesn't apply Burn itself, so aim it at a target that's already carrying debuffs. A 3-turn ultimate cooldown at max level is short, so the grudge keeps coming. Five debuffs on the target is the dream.
prose.passive: Festering Resentment gives +15% ATK and 3 starting Ignition. Every time an ally hits with a Special or Ultimate she gains 1 Ignition, and 1 more if that ally is Sun. She fills Ignition faster in a Sun team. In other words: invite your Sun friends.¶Starting with 3 Ignition means she's closer to her first reaction than most. Specials and Ultimates from allies get her to max quickly, so a team full of those is the best partner.
prose.closing: Level the ultimate first, then the Special. She wants Sun allies and a team that attacks every turn. Great in PvE, and she'll do fine in PvP.
prose.dupes: On dupes: you don't need them. A star is only +2% ATK, HP and DEF, up to +14% at 7 stars. The kit is complete at 0 stars, so spend pieces on a carry only after everything else is done.
prose.play: Let your allies open. As soon as they use Specials or Ultimates, her Ignition climbs and her reaction fires: Burn on the whole enemy team, a big turn gauge boost and Ignition for other Sun allies. Then use the basic (with the chain damage on a debuffed target) and the ultimate to cash in.¶After the reaction, her Ignition resets, so the cycle restarts. Don't waste the ultimate on a clean enemy. Wait for the Burn, then fire it for the Chain DMG. If you have a Nova Burst to spare, the basic's Burn is a decent backup.
prose.gear: Strength first, Vitality second, Focus third. Gear: ATK%, CRIT Rate, CRIT DMG, SPD, Effect Hit (her Burn comes from the reaction, so Effect Hit helps it land before level 8). Attack (4) or Destruction (4) sets, with Precision (4) or Hit (2) if the Burn keeps missing. Upgrade the ultimate first (level 6 cooldown), then the Special (cooldown at level 6, Burn chance at levels 4 and 8, turn progress through the rest), then the passive (levels 2 to 4), then the basic. She wants five key upgrades, so she's expensive to finish.

apostle-tyria.author: Rook
apostle-tyria.take: A Defender-killer with Shatter and DEF penetration. Her passive is called Guillotine Executor. Subtle.

prose.overview: Tyria is an Apostle called "Executor", and her passive is named Guillotine Executor. She doesn't hide it. She marks the enemy with Thorns of Ruin, strips DEF, then slams them with a greatsword. If the enemy is a Defender, the swing does +50% damage. The Defenders are not having a good time.¶The key idea is Thorns. Every one of her attacks either puts Thorns on the enemy, benefits from Thorns, or spends Thorns. Once you understand that, her rotation falls out naturally. She's a solo carry that doesn't need a team to work.
prose.basic: Prelude to the End is 65% ATK and gives her 1 Ignition. Her passive then applies Thorns of Ruin with a 100% chance after it, and 15% to 25% DEF penetration (depending on passive level) applies to the hit if the enemy already has Thorns.¶If the enemy is already at max Thorns after the hit, the passive triggers Requiem of Ruin automatically. So the basic is the engine that feeds the whole kit. The Nova Burst adds 1 Toughness damage.
prose.special: Requiem of Ruin is 70% ATK on one enemy. It gets +10% damage per Thorns stack (the game text is vague on whose stacks), +50% against Defenders and +20% at max Ignition. It removes the target's Thorns afterwards and spends her Ignition. Manual use gives 3 turns of SPD Up. Cooldown 5, then 4 at level 6.¶The extra Requiem the passive fires doesn't give the SPD Up, only a manual cast does. So you'll still press it yourself sometimes. It's the payoff: the bigger the Thorns and Ignition, the bigger the hit.
prose.ult: Crescendo of Sorrow is 160% ATK on all enemies. She gets Shatter for 2 turns and 2 Ignition. Every enemy gets 1 Thorns, and the highest-DEF enemy gets 3. The Nova Burst gives her an extra turn after attacking. Cooldown 6, then 5 at level 6.¶It's a Shatter source, and there are only three in the game. It's also her setup button: the highest-DEF enemy instantly hits max Thorns, so her next basic automatically fires Requiem of Ruin on it.
prose.passive: Guillotine Executor is +15% ATK and 15% to 25% DEF penetration against Thorns targets with Prelude or Requiem. Thorns applies at 100% after Prelude, and it ignores ACC, Effect RES and Immunity. It disappears if she's defeated, so keep her alive.¶The Thorns effect is special: it can't be resisted the way normal debuffs can. That makes her reliable against bosses and immune-heavy PvP teams. Don't extend that to other debuffs though: it's only Thorns.
prose.closing: Great against bosses with a Defender on the field. Level the ultimate first and bring a Shatter-hungry team.
prose.dupes: On dupes: you don't need them. A star is only +2% ATK, HP and DEF, up to +14% at 7 stars. The kit is complete at 0 stars, so spend pieces on a carry only after everything else is done.
prose.play: Open with Crescendo of Sorrow: Shatter, 2 Ignition and Thorns on everyone, with the highest-DEF enemy at max Thorns. Next, use Prelude on that enemy: it gets DEF penetration, adds Ignition and triggers a free Requiem of Ruin.¶Keep using the basic to stack Ignition and Thorns, and cast Requiem manually when Ignition is at max for the +20% bonus and the SPD Up. Against a Defender, aim the Requiem at it for +50%. The ultimate also gives 2 Ignition, so Requiem is already closer to its +20% bonus by the time it fires.
prose.gear: Strength first, Vitality second, Focus third. Gear: ATK%, CRIT Rate, CRIT DMG, SPD. Attack (4) or Destruction (4) sets. Upgrade the ultimate first (level 6 cooldown, plus its +5% damage at the end), then the Special (level 6 cooldown), then the passive (the DEF penetration scales from 15% to 25%), then the basic. Because Thorns ignores resistance, she doesn't need Effect Hit, so spend those stats on crit.

independent-vagabond.author: Rook

prose.overview: Fei's defense plan is "maybe they'll miss". She has 50% evasion every turn, a counter attack when she dodges and an ATK bonus that stacks the more she dodges. It's gambling with a sword. When it works, it looks unfair. When it doesn't, you lose the match you had in the bag.¶What makes her usable is how much her kit pays out for a dodge. She gets ATK, Chill, Sure Hit and a free hit. Over a long fight the odds are in her favor, and 53% of top-100 Gauntlet squads agree.
prose.basic: Lunar Eclipse is 65% ATK and gives her 1 Chill. The Nova Burst gives her ATK Up for 1 turn and adds 1 Toughness damage.¶The basic is where most of her Chill comes from, so use it to build toward max for the ultimate.
prose.special: Lunar Shadow is a reaction at 90% ATK. When Fei dodges an attack she hits the attacker, gets Sure Hit for 1 turn, gains 2 Chill and inflicts ATK Down for 1 turn (75% at first, 85% at level 4, 100% at level 8). No cooldown is listed.¶You don't press it, the enemy does. Each dodge is a counter plus 2 Chill. That's a big chunk of the 5 Chill she needs to power her ultimate.
prose.ult: Silent Wind Lucent Moon is 115% ATK on one enemy. It gives her ATK Up for 2 turns and penetrates 20% of DEF if Chill is at max. It removes all Chill afterwards, even if she wasn't at max. Cooldown 5, then 4 at level 6.¶A payoff to inspect, not a reason to delay every finish. If you can fire it at full Chill, great. If an enemy is about to die, don't wait.
prose.passive: Path of the Celestial Art gives +15% ATK and Evasion Up at battle start and at the end of each turn (50% evasion, not a guarantee). Each successful dodge gives +2% to 4% ATK by passive level, up to 5 stacks. Later levels also add ATK.¶It's the engine of her whole kit. Every dodge feeds her Chill and ATK. Don't treat the 50% as a guarantee. Bring a healer or shielder for the turns when the coin lands wrong.
prose.closing: Level the ultimate first, then the passive. PvP is where she shines, and 53% usage says people noticed. Be ready to lose a match to a dodge you didn't get.
prose.dupes: About dupes: ignore them for now. Stars give flat stat bumps (+2% each, +14% max) and never unlock skills.
prose.play: Use the basic to build Chill while waiting for the enemy to attack. Each dodge gives a free counter, 2 Chill and an ATK stack. When Chill is full, fire the ultimate for the DEF penetration and ATK Up. Then repeat.¶If she isn't dodging, the plan still works: basic, basic, ultimate. It's just slower. Keep a healer or shielder nearby for when the coin flips the wrong way.
prose.gear: Strength first, Vitality second, Focus third. Gear: ATK%, CRIT Rate, CRIT DMG, SPD, with Effect Hit as the fifth stat. Attack (4) or Destruction (4) sets. Upgrade the ultimate first (level 6 cooldown), then the passive (levels 2 to 4 raise the ATK per dodge and her base ATK), then the Special (damage and the ATK Down chance), then the basic.

bunny-knight.author: Rook
bunny-knight.take: A gambler carry whose Special buffs the whole team and ends with an extra turn. The table-flip ult is a bonus.

prose.overview: Heart of Monastir is a bunny knight, and her ultimate is literally called "Cornered Rabbit": she's lost all her chips and flips the table. I love it. She's a Main DPS whose Special is a team buff, which is a weird thing for a carry to do, and a very good one.¶She's built around a simple idea. Fill up Ignition, then dump it into one big hit. Everything in her kit either gives Ignition, gives her extra actions or makes the dump hit harder. A 40% ATK basic that triggers twice and a 90% ATK ultimate don't look scary until you see how many times she gets to use them.
prose.basic: Bunny Step is 40% ATK and gives her 1 Ignition. It also gives her +10% turn progress after she uses it (6% at first). With Lucky Token she triggers it one extra time per turn, so one press is two hits, two Ignition and a lot of turn gauge.¶A 40% ATK basic is nothing on its own. It's the doubling and the Ignition that matter. The Nova Burst adds 1 Toughness damage.
prose.special: Song of the Toast gives all allies ATK Up for 2 turns, gives her Lucky Token for 3 turns, rolls Ignition three times (75% each at first, 100% at level 10) and gives her an extra turn. Cooldown 5, then 4 at level 6. Lucky Token is +20% DEF penetration.¶It's a buff, a setup and a free turn in a single glass raise. Because it also hands the whole team ATK Up, she's a support and a carry in the same move. Don't cast it with nothing to attack afterwards: the extra turn is where the damage happens.
prose.ult: Cornered Rabbit is 90% ATK on one enemy with +5% damage per Ignition (up to 5 stacks, so +25%) and it clears Ignition afterwards. It's also listed to reset its own cooldown at full Ignition, but the game text is vague, so I wouldn't plan around it. Cooldown 6, then 5. The Nova Burst adds 1 Toughness damage and heals her for 30% of the damage dealt.¶The ultimate is a finisher, not an opener. Build Ignition first, then cash in. A 90% ATK hit with +25% is a real attack, but the value is in the setup being nearly free.
prose.passive: Rabbit's Luck is +15% ATK and +1 Ignition whenever a Sun ally (other than her) starts their turn. If she has Lucky Token she throws a bonus Bunny Step after her own Bunny Step, once per turn.¶Bring Sun friends and she gets extra Ignition on their turns, which makes her ultimate bigger. Without them she's still fine, because her Special and basic produce enough Ignition on their own, but she does best in a Sun team.
prose.closing: Level the ultimate first, then the Special. Pair her with other Sun allies and she'll keep the party feeling lucky.
prose.dupes: On dupes: you don't need them. A star is only +2% ATK, HP and DEF, up to +14% at 7 stars. The kit is complete at 0 stars, so spend pieces on a carry only after everything else is done.
prose.play: Open with Song of the Toast: team ATK Up, Lucky Token, up to three Ignition rolls and an extra turn. On that extra turn, use Bunny Step: with Lucky Token it triggers twice, giving 2 more Ignition and a lot of turn gauge. Now you're at or near 5 Ignition.¶Fire Cornered Rabbit for the +25% hit. Then cycle: basic, basic, Special when it's ready. Don't cast the Special without a plan for the extra turn, and don't cast the ultimate at 0 Ignition unless the enemy is about to die.
prose.gear: Strength first, Vitality second, Endurance third. Gear: ATK%, CRIT Rate, CRIT DMG, SPD. Attack (4) or Destruction (4) sets. Upgrade the ultimate first (level 6 cuts the cooldown), then the Special (levels 2 to 10 raise the Ignition roll chance and level 6 cuts its cooldown), then the passive, then the basic. Don't skip the Special: reaching 100% Ignition rolls makes the opening turn much more reliable.

prose.ult: 21st Form: Blade Gale is 115% ATK on one enemy, with a 100% chance to Stun for 1 turn and -20% turn gauge, plus 10% for each Chill stack (up to 5). At full Chill that's -70%. prose.overview: Professor M hits things with a handbag. That is the whole attack animation and I respect it. Don't let the Sub DPS label fool you, because her real job is making your carry hit twice. Every time she uses her basic, she picks your highest-ATK ally and drags them into a free Dual Attack.¶That makes her a force multiplier more than a damage dealer. The better your carry, the better she is. If you only have one strong Special-heavy attacker, she's one of the first characters you should slot beside them.
prose.basic: Black or White is 65% ATK and 1 Chill. The damage is a rounding error. What matters is the passive: right after the basic, the ally with the highest ATK gets Sample Behavior Analysis for 1 turn (+10% damage) and a Dual Attack with Professor M fires immediately.¶So one basic means two attacks on the enemy and a +10% buff on your carry. The Nova Burst adds 1 Toughness damage and 20% turn progress. If you only press one button with her, press this.
prose.special: Evil Begets Evil is a reaction. When she's at max Chill (five stacks) after an ally attacks, she hits the enemy for 70% ATK, fills 15% of her turn gauge (5% at level 1, 15% at level 8) and spends all her Chill. If the enemy's Toughness is broken she does +30% damage.¶You never press it. It fires automatically, favoring the enemy she attacked last. The thing to remember is that your team's attacks are the fuel, so a team that attacks often triggers it often.
prose.ult: The Magic Bullet is 115% ATK on one enemy, gives her 3 Chill (so the reaction is closer to ready), fills 50% of her turn gauge and tries to put Target Engrave on the enemy for 2 turns. The Engrave chance is 75% at first and 100% at max level.¶Target Engrave makes Special skills do 20% more damage to that enemy, and only Special skills. That's perfect if your carry uses a Special as their main button and wasted if they spam basics. Cooldown 5, then 4 at level 6.
prose.passive: Research Subject gives +15% ATK and the Sample mechanic. Each time an ally other than her attacks, she gains 4% turn progress and a chance of 1 Chill (50% rising to 100% by passive level). If the attacking ally has Sample on them, she gets another 4% and another Chill.¶That's a snowball: she attacks, your carry gets Sample, your carry attacks, she gets Chill and speed, and so on. The longer the fight lasts, the faster she runs. A new Sample replaces the old one, so there's only ever one buffed ally.
prose.closing: Great if your carry uses Special skills, and one of the best Sub DPS slots for any team with a single strong attacker. Level the ultimate first.
prose.dupes: Dupes? Optional. Every star adds +2% ATK, HP and DEF (+14% at 7 stars) and never touches the kit, so they are a whale bonus, not a requirement.
prose.play: Turn one, if she's up first: use the basic to start the Dual Attack. If the ultimate is ready and your carry has a Special available, use the ultimate first so the Engrave is on the enemy when your carry's Special lands. Then keep using the basic every turn she isn't using the ultimate.¶Don't hold the ultimate. Its cooldown is short, it refills her Chill and turn gauge, and Engrave lasts only 2 turns. Re-apply it as soon as it's ready. If your carry doesn't have a Special to fire, the ultimate is just a 115% hit with turn progress, which is still fine but not her best.
prose.gear: Strength first, then Vitality, then Focus. Gear: ATK%, CRIT Rate, CRIT DMG, SPD, with Effect Hit as a fifth pick if you can spare it. She benefits from SPD because the more often she acts, the more Dual Attacks you get. Attack (4) or Destruction (4) sets work. Upgrade the ultimate first, since the level 4 and level 8 upgrades raise Engrave chance (+10% then +15%, ending at 100%) and level 6 cuts the cooldown. Then Special (level 4 and 8 raise the turn progress), then passive, then basic.

prose.overview: Gwen is a Lampadis detective who deduces the culprit and then whips them. She's a Sub DPS that doesn't really act like one, because her passive converts your team's attacks into hits of her own. The more your squad does, the more she does. A group project where the one with the whip does the most work.¶Her shtick is simple once you see it: Standby makes her hard to target, allies attacking charge her up, and every 5 charges she fires a free hit. That makes her strong in teams that attack every turn and a bit wasted in teams that don't.
prose.basic: Truth Behind the Whip is 65% ATK and gives her 1 Leap. Leap does a small damage bonus against Moon enemies and, when she doesn't have Standby, it also fuels her turn progress. The Nova Burst adds 1 Toughness damage.¶Use it as a filler. The basic isn't why you play her.
prose.special: Light of Truth! is 70% ATK on one enemy and fills 10% of her turn gauge. When it fires as an extra activation it deals +10% damage. Cooldown 4, then 3 at level 6. The Nova Burst adds 1 Toughness damage and 2 Electric Shock.¶The skill's flavour is "portable truth inducer", which is detective for taser. You'll press it manually sometimes, but most of her Light of Truth! hits come from the passive and the ultimate.
prose.ult: The Culprit Is You! is 115% ATK on one enemy. It triggers 2 Electric Shock on her, gives her On-Site Standby for 3 turns and then triggers Light of Truth! on the enemy. Cooldown 5, then 4 at level 6.¶That's three effects for one button. The Standby part is why she stays alive, the shocks bring her toward a free hit, and the follow-up Light of Truth! is extra damage. It's the button that starts her loop.
prose.passive: Stakeout gives +15% ATK and 1 turn of On-Site Standby at the start of the first battle. While on Standby, every ally attack gives her 1 Electric Shock (1 more if it was a Special). At 5 shocks after an ally attack she spends them to trigger Light of Truth!. Shocks cap at 10.¶Standby stops enemies from selecting her with single-target attacks while another ally lives, but area damage still hits her. When she doesn't have Standby, she gets 2% to 4% turn progress per Leap at the start of ally and enemy turns, so she's never fully idle.
prose.closing: Take her for PvP and for any team full of attackers. Level the ultimate first, since Standby and the free Light of Truth! live there.

At 5 shocks she fires automatically.¶When Standby ends, re-cast the ultimate if it's ready, or use Light of Truth! manually and fall back to Leap-based turn progress. Don't let her sit with 5+ shocks unused: they fire after an ally's next attack, so keep the team attacking.

prose.overview: Scarlet is the tiny tyrant who plays everything as a game and cheats at it. Her passive rolls a few pinball effects at the start of each turn and she gets faster the longer she survives. It's chaotic and surprisingly charming.
prose.basic: Here I Come! is 65% ATK and 1 Ignition.
prose.special: This Doesn't Count! is 70% ATK on one enemy with a guaranteed 2-turn Recovery Down, a buff removal, 1 Ignition and an extra turn. Cooldown 4. It's a very polite way of saying "I get to go again."
prose.ult: Anyway, I Won! is 160% ATK on every enemy with Recovery Down for 2 turns and a 75% chance of 1 turn of SPD Down. It cuts its own cooldown by 1 for each Seven Ball stack she has and resets at 3. Cooldown 5.
prose.passive: High Score! gives +15% CRIT Rate and +7% damage per Ignition (5 max). Each turn she rolls three Pinball Time effects: Normal Balls give 1% damage, Seven Balls give 7% and permanent SPD, which caps at +10 SPD at the top passive level.
prose.closing: Cute and useful against healers. Not essential.
prose.dupes: On dupes: not needed. A star is +2% ATK, HP and DEF and nothing else, so her value comes from the kit at 0 stars.

prose.overview: Luna is a swimsuit tank, and she's the one 87% of top-100 Gauntlet squads picked. White Pearl Trap is the title, and it fits: she punishes enemies for landing a crit. Your carry takes one, Luna steps in, shields up and hits back.¶Crits are how most PvP teams kill carries, and Luna is built to answer exactly that. She makes crits less damaging, makes the enemy weaker for hitting you and forces enemies to look at her. The tank archetype is rarely this proactive.
prose.basic: Bubble Swing! is 60% ATK plus 4.5% max HP and gives her 1 Ignition. The Nova Burst gives her a 1-turn Barrier and 1 more Ignition, plus 1 Toughness damage.¶HP-based damage means HP gear is her damage gear. The basic is how she re-fills Ignition between reactions.
prose.special: Summer Temptation is a reaction with a cooldown of 1. When an ally (not her) is hit by a crit, she hits the attacker for 85% ATK plus 6% max HP, gets a 2-turn Barrier and inflicts DEF Down for 2 turns (100%). At full Ignition it deals +100% damage and Taunts the enemy for 1 turn (75% at first, 100% at max), and spends the Ignition.¶Cooldown 1 means basically every crit. She starts with 5 Ignition, so the first reaction already comes empowered. After that, her passive refills Ignition when crits land on her or her allies.
prose.ult: Welcome to Paradise! is 90% ATK plus 6% max HP on one enemy. It gives all allies DEF Up for 2 turns, gives her 3 Ignition and inflicts ATK Down plus Taunt on the target. Cooldown 5, then 4 at level 6.¶A single button that turns the enemy's best attacker into a punching bag. The 3 Ignition gets her to max again, so the next reaction is boosted. Use it when you need to protect the team or force a hit onto her.
prose.passive: Midsummer Essential gives +15% max HP, 5 Ignition at the start of the first battle and Waterproof Sunscreen for 3 turns to the other allies (+50% CRIT DMG RES). Crits on her give 1 Ignition, and crits on allies give 1 Ignition at 60% chance, rising to 100%.¶The sunscreen is the quiet part of her kit: your whole team takes much less from crits for the first three turns, which is when most PvP matches get decided.
prose.closing: Level the ultimate first, then the Special. A top PvP tank and a decent PvE one. Stack HP and let enemies crit into her.
prose.dupes: On dupes: not needed. A star is +2% ATK, HP and DEF and nothing else, so her value comes from the kit at 0 stars.
prose.play: Open with the ultimate if you want the DEF Up and the Taunt on a dangerous enemy, or just let the reaction fire. She starts with 5 Ignition, so the first crit on an ally triggers the big version: +100% damage, DEF Down and a Taunt.¶After that, use the basic to rebuild Ignition and the ultimate to refill it. In PvE she's a tank who punishes crits. In PvP she's a tank who turns the enemy's best damage dealer into a liability.
prose.gear: Vitality first, Endurance second, Focus third. Gear: HP%, DEF%, SPD, Effect RES. Health (4) or Defense (2) sets, and Speed (4) if she needs to act first. Upgrade the ultimate first (level 6 cooldown cut), then the Special (the Taunt chance rises at levels 4 and 8 to 100%, and damage bumps are large), then the passive, then the basic.

prose.special: Upstream Water Prison is 110% ATK on one enemy with a SPD Up for 2 turns and 1 Agitation. If the target has Entangled Dream, it deals +20% more damage (and the Nova Burst adds another +20%). The cooldown is 3, shorter than most.¶Mark first, hit second. SPD Up on top of 115 SPD means she can act twice before slower enemies act once. It's her main damage button.
prose.ult: Song of Water and Fire is 210% ATK on one enemy, gives her 3 Agitation and ATK Up for 3 turns, then tries to put Entangled Dream on all enemies for 3 turns. The chance is 75% at first, 85% at level 4 and 100% at level 8. The mark cuts enemy ATK by 10%. Cooldown 5, then 4 at level 6.¶This is the button that sets up everything else. The 3 Agitation also pushes her toward max stacks, which feeds her passive. It's both the opener and the way to keep the mark up.
prose.passive: Wish-Bearing Script gives +15% ATK and starts the fight with 2 Agitation. When a marked enemy hits her she gains 1 Agitation, heals (based on her ATK) and moves 6% to 10% closer to her turn. If she's hit at full Agitation by an unmarked enemy, she spends the stacks and tries to put Entangled Dream on it for 2 turns.¶So the more they hit her, the more it helps. Don't let that become a plan. She's a carry, not a tank, so it works best as a safety net.
prose.closing: Level the ultimate first, then the Special. Great for PvE and a fine PvP pick, though the top-100 Gauntlet squads don't run her. Get the mark to 100% at level 8 and she's much smoother.
prose.dupes: Dupes? Optional. Every star adds +2% ATK, HP and DEF (+14% at 7 stars) and never touches the kit, so they are a whale bonus, not a requirement.
prose.play: Open with the ultimate: Entangled Dream on everyone, ATK Up and 3 Agitation. Then use Upstream Water Prison every time it's ready: +20% on marked targets and SPD Up that keeps her ahead. Use the basic to fill gaps.¶Re-cast the ultimate when the mark is about to fall off (it lasts 3 turns). If a marked enemy hits her she gets a bit healthier and faster, which is a bonus, not the plan. With 115 SPD she's often the first to act, so she can reapply the mark before enemies get to use theirs.
prose.gear: Strength first, Vitality second, Focus third. Gear: ATK%, CRIT Rate, CRIT DMG, SPD, with Effect Hit helping Entangled Dream land before level 8. Attack (4) or Destruction (4) sets. Upgrade the ultimate first (level 4 and 8 raise the mark chance, level 6 cuts the cooldown), then the Special, then the passive, then the basic. Her investment is low: only one key upgrade.

prose.overview: Asherah in a ball gown (Waltz of Starlight) is a healer who also attacks, and the game was kind enough to make the attack part of the heal. Her Special is a hit on one enemy and a party-wide heal together, on a 3-turn cooldown. If you've ever wanted to do two jobs at once and have it count, she's it.¶The trick is that her damage is based on HP, so the same stat that keeps the team alive also makes her hit harder. That means one gear set does both jobs, which is what makes her so efficient to build.
prose.basic: Belle Lame is 50% ATK plus 3.5% of her max HP and gives her 1 Insight. From passive level 2 it also heals your lowest-HP ally, and the Nova Burst removes 1 debuff from every ally and adds 1 Toughness damage.¶That means a basic attack can also be a small heal, which is great on a turn when the Special is on cooldown. Every Insight also raises her Dual Attack chance, so the basic is a setup move too.
prose.special: Bal Doré is 55% ATK plus 3.6% max HP on one enemy, heals the whole party and gives her Starlight Wish for 2 turns (10% SPD and 30% Effect RES) plus 1 Insight. Cooldown is 3.¶That's your main button. A 3-turn cooldown on a heal-and-attack combo means you can use it almost every other turn. Recovery rises at levels 2, 3, 6, 8 and 10, damage at levels 4, 5, 7 and 9, so upgrading is spread evenly.
prose.ult: Lumière Sonnet is a party heal, removes 2 debuffs from every ally and gives every other ally +15% turn progress. She also gains 1 Insight. No damage on this one. Cooldown 5, then 4 at level 6.¶Red carpet included, apparently. The turn progress is a real support effect: one cast and your whole team acts sooner. Use it when the team is both hurt and debuffed, or when you want to push your carry's turn forward.

Each Insight stack adds 10% to 20% Dual Attack chance by passive level, up to 5 stacks. At the top that's up to 100% Dual Attack chance, which is silly.¶A Dual Attack means she attacks alongside an ally's attack, so with 5 Insight she's almost always adding damage. Insight comes from every skill, so she builds it naturally. But the passive is much weaker at level 1, so upgrade it.

prose.overview: Carmen's wedding got ruined, so she took up bodyguarding. When the first fight starts she ties an Oath to your highest-ATK ally, and from then on she stands in front of every single-target hit like it owes her money. Eternal Promise is the title and she takes it literally.¶The short version of why she's everywhere: she is a tank, a healer, a shield and a turn-order tool in one slot. 85% of top-100 Gauntlet squads run her. When the people grinding ranks all pick the same support, you can stop asking whether she's worth building and start asking where to put her.
prose.basic: Do Not Disturb is 50% ATK plus 3.5% of her max HP, and it gives her 1 Chill. On paper that's a boring poke. In practice it's her healing button, because her passive heals all allies every time she uses it.¶There's a hidden bonus: if Chill is at max when she uses it, the passive spends all her Chill and the healing is stronger. So the basic is a small heal on a normal turn and a big heal when you've saved up Chill. The Nova Burst version also heals the lowest-HP ally on top and adds 1 Toughness damage.
prose.special: Guardian Knight is a reaction, so you never click it. When the Oath ally is attacked she heals them, puts a 2-turn HP-based Barrier on them and pushes both of you 15% closer to your next turns (30% at max level). She also gets 2 Chill.¶The cooldown is 3, and it drops to 2 at level 6. It fires without a click, so it works even if you're not watching. It also feeds her Chill, which is what powers the big basic heal. A heal, a shield, free tempo and a Chill refill from a button you didn't press: that's why upgrading it first is correct.
prose.ult: Wedding March removes all debuffs from one ally and heals them. If that ally is Moon, they also get 3 Chill. Carmen gets 3 Chill herself. Cooldown 5, then 4 at level 6.¶The description says "allies" but the data says single target, so don't plan a party-wide cleanse. Think of it as an emergency button: poisoned carry, stunned carry, locked-down carry, one press, fixed. The 3 Chill it gives her is the second half of a full basic-heal setup.
prose.passive: Oath gives +15% max HP and does the bodyguard bit. At the start of the first fight the ally with the highest ATK gets Oath of Devotion, which adds Effect RES and sticks through revival. While it's on, Carmen takes 40% of the damage dealt to that ally and gains 30% turn progress whenever that ally eats a single-target attack.¶The catch is the word "highest ATK". The game picks, you don't. If your team has two strong attackers, the stronger one gets the Oath, so line-up matters. And area attacks aren't covered, so a boss that hits everyone will still hurt your carry. Plan for that with a Barrier or DEF Up from a teammate.
prose.closing: Take her. Upgrade Guardian Knight first, put her next to your best attacker and make sure your best attacker has the highest ATK. That's the entire plan.
prose.dupes: On dupes: not needed. A star is +2% ATK, HP and DEF and nothing else, so her value comes from the kit at 0 stars.
prose.play: Open with your carry attacking and let Guardian Knight do its thing. When the Oath ally gets hit, she heals, shields and speeds you both up without your help. On Carmen's own turn, use Wedding March if there's a debuff to clear or if you want Chill for the basic, otherwise use the basic to heal the team.¶The loop is: Guardian Knight adds 2 Chill, Wedding March adds 3, so one of each and you're at max. Then Do Not Disturb heals the whole team for extra and resets Chill. Don't spend the ultimate when nobody needs a cleanse unless you want the Chill. If your Oath ally is a Moon attribute, Wedding March is a double win: debuffs gone and 3 Chill for them.
prose.gear: Build her for HP. Take Vitality first, Endurance second and Strength last in Auto Journey, because her heals, Barrier and damage all scale from max HP. Gear priority is HP%, then DEF%, then SPD, then Effect RES. A Health set (4) is the safe choice, and Speed (4) if you want her acting before the enemy. Upgrade Guardian Knight first, since level 6 drops the cooldown from 3 to 2 and level 8 pushes the turn progress up. Then the ultimate (level 6 cooldown cut), then the passive, then the basic. Basic upgrades only add 1% to 2% damage each, so skip them.

Amora strikes with a spear you can't see, leaps down with her Special and wraps up with an execution that gives her another turn. It's a simple plan: hit, hit, extra turn, nobody asks questions.¶The reason she's S+ in PvP is her passive. Debuffs are how opponents beat carries, and Amora both hits harder without them and cleans them off herself. She's a carry who punishes the exact tools people use to stop carries.
prose.basic: The Ever-Sober Spear is 65% ATK and gives her 1 Insight. Sober, clean, no debuffs. That's the whole theme.¶Insight adds a small stacking damage bonus against Chaos enemies, and it also fuels her passive cleanse. The Nova Burst adds 1 Toughness damage.
prose.special: Piercing Star is 100% ATK on one enemy with a 100% chance of ACC Down for 1 turn, +30% turn progress at max level (15% at first) and 1 Insight. If she has Nocturnal Bloom, it cuts its own cooldown by 1. The base cooldown is 3, which is short enough to run most turns.¶ACC Down makes enemies miss more, which is why it works as a defensive tool. With Bloom on, the cooldown effectively drops to 2, so she can throw it nearly every other turn.
prose.ult: Light-Forged Execution is 265% ATK on all enemies, gives her 3 turns of Nocturnal Bloom (extra SPD and 20% DEF penetration), applies ACC Down for 2 turns (75% at first, 100% at max) and gives her an extra turn. Cooldown 6.¶The extra turn is the big deal: she casts the ultimate and immediately acts again with Bloom up, which makes the follow-up Piercing Star cheaper. This is the one where she says "sentence" and means it.
prose.passive: Master of Stranis gives +15% ATK and +30% damage while she has no debuffs. If she gets hit while debuffed she gains 3 Insight, and at max Insight she cleans every debuff off herself at the start of her turn and gets ATK Up and Nocturnal Bloom for 2 turns.¶Being debuffed turns into a setup, not a problem. In PvP, debuff-heavy teams will find her annoying. Keep an eye on the +30% though: if she's debuffed at the moment she attacks, she loses it.
prose.closing: A simple, powerful carry. Level the ultimate first, then the Special, and she'll hold her own in PvE and PvP.
prose.dupes: Dupes? Optional. Every star adds +2% ATK, HP and DEF (+14% at 7 stars) and never touches the kit, so they are a whale bonus, not a requirement.
prose.play: Ultimate first when it's ready, because it gives Bloom, an extra turn and DEF penetration. With Bloom running, throw Piercing Star on cooldown (it cuts its own cooldown) and use the basic to fill gaps. If she takes a debuff, let the passive clean it at turn start, and avoid attacking while debuffed if you can.¶The ultimate cooldown is the longest part of the loop. Plan around it: two Piercing Stars and a couple of basics fit between each ultimate. If an enemy has a lot of debuff tools, bring a teammate with a cleanse.
prose.gear: Strength first, Vitality second, Focus third. Gear: ATK%, CRIT Rate, CRIT DMG, SPD, with Effect Hit optional. Attack (4) or Destruction (4) sets. Upgrade the ultimate first: levels 4 and 8 raise the ACC Down chance (+10%, then +15%, ending at 100%) and the damage bumps are the biggest of her skills (+5% at level 10). Then the Special (levels 4 and 8 raise turn progress), then the passive. She has no cooldown cut on any skill, so upgrades are about damage and chance.

prose.overview: Sharp & Sweet is a maid, so her attack is called Dust Buster and her ultimate is called Maid's Special. I don't make the rules. She heals the whole party, cleans debuffs and hands out ATK Up, and a free bonus heal falls out of her passive every few turns. It's a cleaning service that actually shows up.¶What makes her better than a plain healer is that every action she takes feeds the next one. Skills give Dust Detection, ally turns give Dust Detection, and at 5 stacks the game gives you a free extra heal. You get more value the longer the fight runs.
prose.basic: Dust Buster is 40% ATK and gives her 1 Ignition. It's a small number and it doesn't matter. The Nova Burst adds 1 Toughness damage, which is plenty for a healer.¶Basic upgrades only add around 1% damage each, so don't spend materials here. Use it on turns when both skills are on cooldown and nobody needs help.
prose.special: Pre-Arrival Cleanup heals every ally from her max HP and gives Refreshing Mood for 1 turn, a heal that ticks at the start of their turn. She gains 1 Ignition. When it fires as a bonus cast on her own turn it also removes 1 debuff from every ally. If she's at max Ignition on that bonus cast, the healing gets +30% and the Ignition is spent. Cooldown 4, then 3 at level 6.¶It's the skill that does most of the work. A 4-turn cooldown is short for a party heal, and the level 6 cut to 3 makes it close to every other turn. Refreshing Mood stacks, so back-to-back casts build a heal-over-time.
prose.ult: Maid's Special heals all allies, removes 1 debuff from each and gives ATK Up for 2 turns (3 with the Nova Burst). She also gains 1 Dust Detection and 1 Ignition. Cooldown 5, then 4.¶Heal, cleanse and a team-wide damage buff in one button is a lot to ask from a woman holding a duster. Use it when the team is hurt or debuffed, or when your carry is about to cast their ultimate and you want the +ATK on it.
prose.passive: Service with Heart gives +15% max HP. She gains 1 Dust Detection each time she uses a skill and each time another ally starts their turn. At 5 Dust Detection her next skill also triggers a bonus Pre-Arrival Cleanup, and it doesn't give her Dust Detection or Ignition.¶Allies who start their turn with a debuff give her 1 Ignition, and an area attack gives her 18% turn progress (30% at max level) plus Ignition. Being hit by an area attack is actually a good thing for her: she gets to go sooner and charges her bonus heal.
prose.closing: Build her tanky, level the Special first and plug her into any team that wants a healer with a buff. She's the one you can drop in blind.
prose.dupes: About dupes: don't chase them. Seven stars give +14% ATK, HP and DEF in total and no new skills.
prose.play: She's a metronome. Cast Pre-Arrival Cleanup when it's ready, Maid's Special when the team is hurt or when you want ATK Up, and the basic when nothing else is available. After a few ally turns, her Dust Detection reaches 5 and the next skill she uses fires a bonus heal for free.¶The bonus cast is strongest with full Ignition: +30% healing and the cleanse. If you can, save the bonus for a moment when the team has debuffs. Don't feel bad about letting the cooldown tick if nobody's hurt. The passive will stack up anyway.
prose.gear: Vitality first, then Endurance, then Strength. Gear: HP%, SPD, Effect RES, DEF%. The healing is proportional to max HP, so every point of HP is more recovery. A Health (4) set is the safe pick. Upgrade the Special first, because level 6 drops its cooldown from 4 to 3 and recovery rises along the way. Then the ultimate (level 6 cooldown cut), then the passive, then the basic. Skip basic upgrades entirely.

prose.overview: Candle Square Claire is the SR cousin of the Bunny Claire. She has a spear, a very neat bow and a kit that boils down to "hit things, go again." She's fine at the start and quickly overshadowed.

prose.passive: Punctuality is +3 to 12% ATK.
prose.closing: Use her early, bench her later.

counterside-rosaria.overview: Fallen Hawk, Rosaria. Her ultimate description reads "swings her sword to cleave a planet", and the planet is, frankly, not ready. She's a Chaos Ranger with a built-in death refusal and a very clean damage loop.¶The reason people love her isn't one big number, it's that every skill feeds the next one. The basic builds Agitation, Agitation raises Inferno chance, Inferno boosts the Special, and the ultimate refills Inferno. If you pull one carry, I'd pull her.
counterside-rosaria.watch: Wants good crit gear before she feels busted

counterside-rosaria.author: Rook
counterside-rosaria.take: A planet-cleaving nuke with a "no, you can't kill me" passive. One of the strongest carries in the game.

prose.overview: Fallen Hawk, Rosaria. Her ultimate description reads "swings her sword to cleave a planet", and the planet is, frankly, not ready. She's a Chaos Ranger with a built-in death refusal and a very clean damage loop.¶The reason people love her isn't one big number, it's that every skill feeds the next one. The basic builds Agitation, Agitation raises Inferno chance, Inferno boosts the Special, and the ultimate refills Inferno. If you pull one carry, I'd pull her.
prose.basic: Ashen Inferno is 50% ATK and gives her 1 Agitation. Her passive then adds +20% chance per Agitation stack (up to 5 stacks, so up to 100%) of gaining an Inferno stack after she uses it. So the basic isn't filler, it's the Inferno generator.¶The Nova Burst adds 1 Toughness damage. Spamming the basic until the Special is ready is not a mistake, it's the plan.
prose.special: Ruler's Judgement is 90% ATK on one enemy and it spends all your Inferno. 1 stack gives +10% damage, 2 stacks give +20%, and 3 stacks give +20% plus an automatic Ashen Inferno on top. It also gives her 1 Agitation. Cooldown 4, then 3 at level 6.¶The skill is a payoff, not a starter. Don't fire it at 0 Inferno unless you have to. At 3 stacks it's both the strongest hit and a free extra attack.
prose.ult: Difference in Class is 320% ATK on all enemies with a 100% DEF Down for 2 turns (75% at first, 85% at level 4, 100% at level 8). It gives her +50% turn progress and Owner of the Throne for 3 turns, which boosts her basic damage and SPD. Each enemy that takes a critical hit gives her an Inferno, up to 3. Cooldown 6, then 5.¶That last line is the engine. A full-room crit means 3 Inferno on one button, and the Nova Burst gives her +30% CRIT Rate on the hit, so it's easier to land. Open with this, then use the Special at 3 stacks.
prose.passive: Tyrant of the North gives +15% ATK, extra Inferno chance per Agitation, and the clause that makes people mad in PvP: her HP can't drop below 40% when she takes damage, once per battle. If she ends that hit at 40% or below, she gains ATK Up for 1 to 3 turns depending on passive level.¶Think of it as one free "you should be dead" hit per fight. Use it. A smart opponent can't finish her until it's spent, which makes her a great anchor in PvP. Past that point she's an ordinary carry again, so keep a healer close.
prose.closing: Level the ultimate first, then the Special. Build crit, bring a support who keeps her alive past the first clause, and enjoy the planet.
prose.dupes: About dupes: ignore them for now. Stars give flat stat bumps (+2% each, +14% max) and never unlock skills.
prose.play: Turn one, ultimate if it's available: DEF Down on everyone, 50% turn progress, and as many Inferno as the crits give you. Then use basic attacks to stack Agitation and Inferno while the Special's cooldown is down. When you have 3 Inferno, fire the Special for the 20% bonus and the free Ashen Inferno.¶Then repeat. The ultimate's cooldown (5 at level 6) is long enough that you'll do two or three rotations between casts. Don't waste the 50% turn gauge: the faster she acts, the more often she gets to cycle.
prose.gear: Strength first, Vitality second, Focus third. Gear: ATK%, CRIT Rate, CRIT DMG, SPD, and Effect Hit if you have room. Crit is the key stat: the ultimate gives her Inferno per critical hit, and the Nova Burst adds +30% CRIT Rate, so every point of Crit Rate is more Inferno. Upgrade the ultimate first (level 4 and 8 raise DEF Down chance, level 6 cuts cooldown), then the Special (level 6 cooldown), then the passive and the basic.
